{{Short description|Two-dimensional packing problem}}

'''Circle packing in a right isosceles triangle''' is a [[packing problem]] where the objective is to pack {{mvar|n}} [[unit circle]]s into the smallest possible [[Special right triangles#45–45–90_triangle|isosceles right triangle]].

Minimum solutions (lengths shown are length of leg) are shown in the table below.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hydra.nat.uni-magdeburg.de/packing/crt/crt.html|title=The best known packings of equal circles in an isosceles right triangle|first=Eckard|last=Specht|date=2011-03-11|access-date=2011-05-01}}</ref>  Solutions to the equivalent problem of maximizing the minimum distance between {{mvar|n}} [[point (geometry)|points]] in an isosceles right triangle, were known to be [[Mathematical optimization|optimal]] for {{math|''n'' < 8}}<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Xu | first1 = Y. | title = On the minimum distance determined by n (≤ 7) points in an isoscele right triangle | doi = 10.1007/BF02007736 | journal = Acta Mathematicae Applicatae Sinica | volume = 12 | issue = 2 | pages = 169–175 | year = 1996 | s2cid = 189916723 }}</ref> and were extended up to {{math|1=''n'' = 10}}.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Harayama |first=Tomohiro |date=2000 |title=Optimal Packings of 8, 9, and 10 Equal Circles in an Isosceles Right Triangle |publisher=Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology|hdl=10119/1422 }}</ref>

In 2011 a [[heuristic algorithm]] found 18 improvements on previously known optima, the smallest of which was for {{math|1=''n'' = 13}}.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = López | first1 = C. O. | last2 = Beasley | first2 = J. E. | title = A heuristic for the circle packing problem with a variety of containers | doi = 10.1016/j.ejor.2011.04.024 | journal = European Journal of Operational Research | volume = 214 | issue = 3 | pages = 512 | year = 2011 }}</ref>
